patches.scope_notes: Computational methods, software and research delivering substantial biological insight, including genomics and systems biology. Experimental validation is not mandatory; real-world data and reproducibility remain important. Strong conceptual and methodological novelty is required. OSRI fit is existing-data research, theory, simulation or methods/software; check article-type rules for reviews. AI can support research and manuscript development, but ideas, interpretation and accountability remain human; substantive AI use needs tool/use/validation disclosure, while language editing has an exemption. AI tools cannot serve as reviewers or evaluate submissions on behalf of editors/reviewers. Follow the journal ethical-publishing policy.

patches.scope_notes: Computational molecular biology and genome bioinformatics, especially algorithms, databases and software. Original papers generally require actual biological data; simulation-only work needs exceptional justification. Application Notes describe substantive usable software/services, with free noncommercial availability and two-year availability requirements. Reviews are mostly commissioned; prospective authors first send a short proposal. Existing-data methods fit OSRI. The journal permits disclosed LLM research/code assistance and correction/translation, but prohibits drafting papers from prompts; researchers must write the paper and take responsibility. Follow the journal-specific disclosure policy as well as OUP policy.

difficulty.basis: Provisional agent judgment within molecular bioinformatics, supported by the official author guide reporting that approximately 30% of submitted manuscripts are accepted and describing significance-based screening before external review. The statement has no measurement year, reporting interval or raw counts; it must not be presented as a 2026 rate or personal probability. Actual biological data and substantive software/method contribution gates also apply. Citation rank does not determine this band. Recheck the undated source before manuscript-specific decisions.

metrics.name: Journal Impact Factor
metrics.population: Citations during 2025 to journal articles in the preceding two calendar years (2023-2024); raw citation and article-denominator counts are not disclosed on the journal page.

patches.scope_notes: A multidisciplinary journal with a Mathematical and Computational Biology community and relevant genomics, ecology and evolutionary-biology communities. Theory, computer or mathematical models, existing-data studies and methodological work can fit the selected community. Articles must first complete the thematic Peer Community In review and recommendation process; the journal does not take an unevaluated manuscript directly. The final journal step publishes the recommended version without another peer-review round; review provenance comes from the thematic PCI, not from preprint deposit alone.

route.conditions: No submission or publication fees. Software must meet research-impact, feature-completeness and open-development gates, including more than six months of active public development under current pre-review criteria. Major-contributor authors participate through GitHub; archive the reviewed release with a DOI using a free archive. Disclose AI tools, use and human validation. AI use in conversational interactions between authors and editors/reviewers is prohibited except translation. Human authors must make core design decisions and take responsibility.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None charged by the journal; use free code hosting and software archiving. No mandatory author membership or registration charge is stated.

fee_evidence.note: Direct HTTPS readback (HTTP 200) explicitly excludes submission/publication fees and requires DOI archiving after review; browser text extraction omitted the fee subsection.
Direct HTTPS readback (HTTP 200) excludes all manuscript-processing/publication fees and describes free author service; listed publisher operating costs are not author charges.

patches.scope_notes: A cross-disciplinary research-software journal explicitly covering biology and scientific modelling/data analysis. A substantive, reusable computational-biology package can fit. Papers describe software and its research purpose rather than presenting new biological research results. Standalone notebooks, pretrained models and minor utility packages are outside the stated scope. Both software and the accompanying paper receive open external peer review. Current pre-review gates require more than six months of active public history and demonstrated research use; prospective usefulness alone is insufficient. AI-assisted code/paper work needs disclosure and human validation, and AI use in conversational interactions with editors/reviewers is prohibited except translation.

notes: Coverage: read all four completed source-role files and reviewed all 15 merged records, including each route, review type, formats, scope, difficulty and metrics array. This reviewer is a fifth distinct agent. Patches are field replacements and preserve unchanged fee/metric evidence from prior roles.

Independent live checks: all eight Springer journal homepages, aims/scope pages and submission guidelines; Journal of Mathematical Biology publishing-route page plus Springer compulsory-charge support policy; PLOS journal information, editorial process, ethical-publishing policy and central fees; Bioinformatics author guide, About metrics and OUP metric definitions; BIOMATH About/submission material; Biometrical Letters author guide and official platform issues/metrics; Biodiversity Informatics About and author information; PCJ About plus PCI homepage; JOSS About/submission instructions. All checked 2026-11-16. This is not a repeat of every fee-auditor page or a reconstruction of citation numerators.

Financial result remains five verified_free diamond/software pathways, eight needs_verification subscription pathways and two conditional APC-support pathways. No selective waiver, institutional agreement, optional society discount or absent fee statement was promoted to unconditional free publication.

Replaced nine insufficiently calibrated difficulty objects with unknown, including PLOS very_high. Molecular Modeling retains high from its explicit high-rejection warning and concrete validation gates. Bioinformatics retains an expressly limited high judgment with the newly found undated approximate 30% submitted-manuscript statement. Final difficulty distribution: two high, eleven unknown, two not_comparable. These are agent judgments, not individual probabilities.

All eight Springer metric displays matched their retained 2025 JIF/five-year values and undated first-decision medians. Independently checked OUP 2025 values/cohort definitions, BIOMATH reported figures and Biometrical Letters undated platform values. Did not reconstruct bibliometric populations, adopt unidentified PLOS metric cards, derive a BIOMATH rate from counts, complement rejection into acceptance, or assign retrieval year to undated statistics. No null-value metric placeholders were present.

Material corrections: BIOMATH publisher changed in 2022; Molecular Modeling indefinitely excludes Review submissions from 2026-01-01 and has Software Reports; Bioinformatics has restrictive prompt-drafting rules, mostly commissioned Reviews and an undated approximate acceptance statement; JOSS forbids AI correspondence except translation; Biometrical Letters and PLOS have explicit AI disclosure/human responsibility rules. Financial eligibility remains separate from these scholarly restrictions.

Browser/direct-HTTPS accessibility differs: direct OUP and PLOS fees requests returned 403 while browser policy extraction succeeded; PCJ browser returned 403 while direct official-page readback succeeded. Biometrical Letters platform sections and JOSS fee sections sometimes require direct HTML readback. These access details are not evidence of missing policies.

No clinical practice or new physical laboratory work is proposed. Existing-data work, theory, simulation, synthesis and research software must still meet scientific and ethical requirements. Independent agent policy review does not replace human scientific review, and no venue was contacted or manuscript submitted.
